name: SELLERS, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Alabama's "stop and identify" statute, § 15-5-30, empowers officers to demand physical identification when a suspect provides an incomplete or unsatisfactory oral response to verify their identity during a lawful Terry stop.

name: BRYAN, Justice
description: Concurred, agreeing with the main opinion and the sentiments expressed in Justice Shaw's special writing.

name: COOK, Justice
description: Concurred, arguing that the statute does not prohibit, and in fact authorizes, officers to demand physical identification when oral responses are incomplete or unsatisfactory.

name: SHAW, J.
description: Concurred in the result, arguing that the statute allows officers to demand a person's actual name and address, and does not limit the response to oral answers, thus permitting demands for physical identification if oral responses are nonresponsive.

name: MENDHEIM, Justice
description: Dissented, arguing that the court should have declined to answer the certified question due to principles of comity with federal courts, despite agreeing with the majority's interpretation of the statute.

name: Mitchell, J.
description: Concurred, but expressed concern that precedents applying Article I, § 13, to common-law remedies might conflict with its original public meaning, which was to guard against corruption of justice.

name: Parker, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Alabama Constitution's "Sanctity of Unborn Life Amendment" mandates upholding the sanctity of unborn life, including extrauterine life, based on theological principles that human life bears God's image from conception.

name: Shaw, J.
description: Concurred, argued that "minor child" under Alabama law includes all unborn children, whether in vitro or in utero, and that prior common-law prohibitions on wrongful-death actions for unborn children have been superseded by state law and constitutional policy.

name: Stewart, J.
description: Concurred, joining Justice Shaw's special concurrence.

name: Mendheim, J.
description: Concurred in the result, argued that while the Wrongful Death of a Minor Act can be construed to include frozen embryos, the main opinion's assertion of "clear" black-letter law is problematic given the historical context and novelty of IVF.

name: Sellers, J.
description: Dissented in part and concurred in the result in part, argued that the case is about obtaining punitive damages for negligently destroyed frozen embryos, not black-letter law, and that the Brody Act was not intended to include IVF embryos.

name: Cook, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the court overstepped its judicial role by expanding the meaning of the Wrongful Death Act beyond its 1872 original public meaning without legislative amendment, and that this decision will likely end IVF in Alabama.

name: WISE, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the issue of interpreting 'not less than three-fifths of a quorum present' is a nonjusticiable political question, deferring to the legislature's power to determine its own rules.

name: Mitchell, J.
description: Concurred, argued that political questions should lead to dismissal on the merits, not for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction, and that the court should determine if the legislature's interpretation falls within the bounds of its discretion.

name: Parker
description: Concurred in part and concurred in the result, argued that Kelly Walker had standing to challenge the local-tax act's constitutionality under Section 105, and that this claim should have been addressed on its merits, disagreeing with the presumption of constitutionality for Section 105 claims.

name: Mitchell
description: Concurred in part and concurred in the result, argued that the local-tax act does not require distribution to the Gulf Shores Board and that the argument regarding the tax violating Section 105 of the Alabama Constitution, while properly before the court, is without merit.

name: Bryan, J.
description: Concurred, argued that while Dixon's regulatory taking claim is not viable under current Alabama law, the precedent on regulatory takings (Town of Gurley) was wrongly decided and should be overruled.

name: Wise, J.
description: Concurred, joined Justice Bryan's special concurrence.

name: Mendheim, J.
description: Concurred, joined Justice Bryan's special concurrence.

name: BOLIN, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the jury-waiver provision in the PSA is enforceable based on the Gaylord factors, Warren Averett's breach made the arbitration provision "unenforceable" as contemplated by the jury-waiver clause, and the motion to strike is not barred by laches as Fagan showed no prejudice from the delay.

name: MITCHELL, Justice
description: Concurred specially, arguing that the Gaylord factors for jury-trial waivers should be re-evaluated, particularly the 'buried deep in a long contract' factor and the 'intelligently and knowingly made' factor, as they are out of step with contract law principles.

name: PARKER, Chief Justice
description: Dissented, arguing that the constitutional right to a jury trial requires narrow construction of waivers, and the previous decision did not declare the arbitration provision "unenforceable" as required to trigger the jury-waiver, thus the court's decision infringes on Fagan's right to a jury trial.

name: MITCHELL, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the trial court correctly denied Pinkard's immunity claims and that the previous ruling in Barnhart v. Ingalls, which incorrectly expanded state immunity, should be overruled.

name: Parker, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the court's decision correctly re-establishes the test for state immunity, focusing on whether a judgment directly affects a State's contract or property rights, correcting the misinterpretation from Barnhart.

name: Shaw, J.
description: Concurred, argued that while Barnhart's standard for immunity may have been overbroad, Section 14 can still bar suits against individual state employees if the claims are, in substance, against the State, but that Pinkard's claims do not meet this threshold.

name: Sellers, J.
description: Concurred, argued that while Barnhart's standard for immunity may have been overbroad, Section 14 can still bar suits against individual state employees if the claims are, in substance, against the State, but that Pinkard's claims do not meet this threshold.

name: MITCHELL, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the trial court correctly dismissed the action based on state immunity, as neither statute cited by claimants imposed a legal duty on the Governor to continue participation in federal unemployment programs.

name: STEWART, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the local act and ordinance are constitutional as they do not violate §§ 89, 104, or 105 of the Alabama Constitution.

name: Mendheim, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the local act does not violate § 104(14) because red-light violations are civil, and does not violate § 89 as it merely enlarges upon state general laws, but dissented from the main opinion's rationale for upholding the local act under § 105's "demonstrated local need" exception.

name: Mitchell, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the local act does not cover the same "case" or "matter" as statewide law under § 105, and that the "local need" exception is judicially created and unnecessary.

name: Parker, C.J.
description: Dissented, argued that the local act addresses the same subject as general law and that the City failed to demonstrate a specifically local need for red-light cameras, thus violating § 105.

name: BRYAN
description: Concurred, argued that the Jefferson County Board of Education is entitled to State immunity under Section 14 of the Alabama Constitution, which provides absolute immunity to the State and its agencies, and therefore the action against it must be dismissed.

name: MITCHELL, Justice
description: Authored the main opinion, holding the Local Act constitutional as it covers distinct matters from general laws, and further argued that courts should interpret the Alabama Constitution according to its original public meaning.

name: Parker, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the term "appropriation" in the main opinion is a generic word for directing tax revenue and should not be interpreted as having bearing on other constitutional challenges.

name: Mendheim, J.
description: Concurred with Part B of the analysis and the result.

name: Shaw, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Local Act does not conflict with a general law, only a presumption of county commission discretion, which is not prohibited by § 105.

name: Bolin, J.
description: Dissented, concurring with Justice Sellers' argument that the Local Act violates § 105.

name: Sellers, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Local Act violates § 105 because the matter regulated by the Local Act is already provided for by the general SSUT Act and Budget Control Act.

name: SELLERS
description: Concurred, but argued that the Act might violate constitutional principles if a biological father's parental rights can be extinguished unilaterally by a mother marrying another man immediately before the child's birth.

name: Bolin
description: Concurred with Justice Sellers' special writing.

name: PARKER, C.J.
description: Concurred in the result, but argued that a compelling textual argument could be made that the AUPA's definition of "child" includes unborn children, and he would not conclusively hold that unborn children are excluded.

name: BRYAN
description: Concurred in the result, but agreed with the sentiments expressed by Justice Sellers in his special writing.

name: SHAW
description: Dissented, argued that the plain language of the AUPA does not exclude an unborn child from the definition of "child" and therefore the Court of Civil Appeals' decision should not be affirmed.

name: MITCHELL
description: Dissented, argued that the AUPA's definition of "child" includes an unborn child.

name: MITCHELL, Justice
description: Concurred, arguing that State immunity bars retrospective monetary relief and attorneys lack third-party standing to assert indigent defendants' constitutional rights.

name: Sellers, J.
description: Concurred in the result, arguing that immunity defenses should be resolved before class certification to promote judicial economy and efficiency.
